title: Branch register
description: The register of the repository's branches: what each one is for, what it sits under, and whether its work has been merged higher, which is what says a branch may be deleted. Not a manifest: a manifest's rows point at units you can open, and a branch lives in git rather than in a file, so no row has a path. Named REGISTER-branches.json for that reason, and typed branch-register for what it is.

kind.description: the words branch-register, which is what chooses this schema

version.description: the shape of this file, counted up when the shape changes

updated.description: the date the register was last checked against the repository, YYYY-MM-DD

rule.description: the standing rule this register exists to enforce, in one line

branches.description: one row per branch. Called branches and not units on purpose: a unit is a file you can open, and these are not

items.description: one branch: what it is called, what it is for, what it sits under and whether its work is safe

name.description: the branch name exactly as git holds it, which may carry slashes and is therefore a free string and never a cockpit name

role.description: what the branch is for, in one line

parent.description: the branch this one was cut from and merges back into; absent for a root branch

merged_higher.description: true only when every commit is contained in a branch above; this, and never the prose of status, is the fact that licenses deleting a branch, and absent means unknown, which is not safe

status.description: where the branch stands, in the register's own words: working line, held, pending decision, candidate with the suite merge. Prose on purpose — the machine-readable fact is merged_higher, and flattening these onto a short enum would be a judgement about the repository, not a shape

note.description: anything the other fields cannot carry
